BasePK: 3563485
Chunk index: 0

Speech chunk:
Mr. Speaker, my question is directed to the Minister of State for Small Businesses. When it was announced that Hyundai would be establishing a plant at Bromont, it was quite clear at the time that the federal Government had agreed with the Government of Quebec to provide a measure of financial participation in this undertaking. Today I want to give the Minister a chance to stop "frigging" around and to inform the House outright whether or not the commitment made by the Prime Minister in his call from Florida will be met and whether we now have the assurance that Hyundai will come to Bromont, with federal participation.

Mr. Speaker, I should like to address a question to the Minister for International Trade responsible for the creation of unemployment in Canada. Could the Minister explain what happened to prevent the Government from honouring the commitment made by the Prime Minister in Sherbrooke when he said that he would maintain the quotas in the footwear industry and thus save 20,000 jobs? What happened that made the Prime Minister cheat the people of Canada?

BasePK: 3563524

Speech chunk:
Mr. Speaker, my question is directed to the Minister of Indian Affairs and Northern Development. I am sure the Minister is aware that the Council of the Haida nation have had their aboriginal claim to the Queen Charlotte Islands accepted by the Department of Justice and by the Minister's Department for over two years. But the B.C. courts have warned the Indian people that they are sleeping on their rights right now. Those Haida people standing up for their rights are now being arrested. Will the Minister appoint a negotiator who can legally and formally get negotiations under way, in order to defuse a very dangerous situation in British Columbia?

Mr. Speaker, I have the honour and responsibility to present two petitions. The first is signed by some 300 members of the Newfoundland and Labrador Federation of Labour who protest the proposed changes in the Unemployment Insurance Act coming into effect January 1, 1986. These changes would have pension income counted as earned income for unemployment insurance purposes. They call upon the Government to retreat from that very retrograde step before it is too late.
